title: Two- and three-word verbs: word order
summary: Порядок слов во фразовых и предложных глаголах: местоимение внутри разделяемого глагола, длинное дополнение после частицы, неразделяемые глаголы (**look after, put up with, run out of**).
ru:
## Четыре типа составных глаголов
Порядок слов зависит от того, к какому типу относится глагол. Сначала определите тип, потом решайте, где стоит дополнение.
1. **Фразовые глаголы с дополнением, разделяемые** (verb + particle): **turn down** an offer, **pick up** the phone, **put off** a meeting, **fill in** a form, **look up** a word.
2. **Фразовые глаголы без дополнения** (непереходные): **take off** (самолёт), **break down**, **show up**, **calm down**.
3. **Предложные глаголы** (verb + preposition): **look after** the children, **depend on** luck, **get over** an illness, **run into** a friend. Дополнение — всегда после предлога.
4. **Трёхсловные глаголы** (verb + particle + preposition): **put up with**, **look forward to**, **run out of**, **get away with**, **come up with**, **look down on**, **get on with**. Дополнение — всегда в конце.

## Разделяемые: существительное — по выбору, местоимение — в середину
Если дополнение — существительное, можно поставить его после частицы или внутрь:
> She **turned down** the offer. = She **turned** the offer **down**. — Она отклонила предложение.
> Could you **switch off** the lights? = Could you **switch** the lights **off**?
Если дополнение — **местоимение** (it, them, him, her, me, us), оно **обязательно** стоит внутри:
> She turned **it** down. (~~She turned down it.~~)
> I'll pick **them** up at six. — Я заберу их в шесть.
> Please fill **it** in. (~~fill in it~~)

## Длинное дополнение — после частицы
Когда дополнение длинное или содержит придаточное, его обычно ставят после частицы: так легче читать.
> The manager **brought up** the issue that had been ignored for years. — Менеджер поднял вопрос, который годами игнорировали.
> ~~The manager brought the issue that had been ignored for years up.~~ — грамматично, но неудобно.
Короткие существительные можно ставить как угодно: *call off the match / call the match off*.

## Неразделяемые: дополнение только после
Предложные и трёхсловные глаголы не разделяются даже местоимением.
> We're looking **after** them. (~~We're looking them after.~~)
> They didn't put **up with** it. (~~put it up with~~)
> We ran **out of** milk. — Is there any left? — No, we ran **out of** it yesterday. (~~We ran out it of.~~)
Есть небольшая группа трёхсловных глаголов, у которых два дополнения: **put sth down to sb/sth** (объяснять чем-то), **take sb up on** (принять предложение), **let sb in on** (посвятить в секрет). В них первое дополнение (местоимение) стоит между глаголом и частицей: *I'll take you up on that offer.* — Принимаю ваше предложение.

## Определяем разделяемость и придаточные
- Хороший тест: подставьте *it*. Если *turn it down* звучит нормально — глагол разделяемый; если *look it after* — нет.
- Есть пары, где один и тот же глагол в двух значениях ведёт себя по-разному: *He ran up the hill* (предлог, не разделяется) и *He ran up a huge bill* (фразовый, возможно: *ran a huge bill up*).
- В вопросах и относительных придаточных частица или предлог остаётся при глаголе: *What are you looking for?* — *the offer we turned down* — *the problem we came up against.*
- В пассиве частица остаётся при глаголе: *The offer was turned down.* — *The children are looked after by their grandmother.*

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~She turned down it.~~ → She turned **it** down.
- ~~He picked up her.~~ → He picked **her** up.
- ~~look them after~~ → look **after them**
- ~~We ran out it of.~~ → We ran **out of** it.
- ~~I can't put up it with.~~ → I can't put **up with it**.
en:
## Four types of multi-word verbs
Word order depends on the type of verb. First decide which type you have, then decide where the object goes.
1. **Separable phrasal verbs** (verb + particle with an object): **turn down** an offer, **pick up** the phone, **put off** a meeting, **fill in** a form, **look up** a word.
2. **Phrasal verbs with no object** (intransitive): **take off** (a plane), **break down**, **show up**, **calm down**.
3. **Prepositional verbs** (verb + preposition): **look after** the children, **depend on** luck, **get over** an illness, **run into** a friend. The object always comes after the preposition.
4. **Three-word verbs** (verb + particle + preposition): **put up with**, **look forward to**, **run out of**, **get away with**, **come up with**, **look down on**, **get on with**. The object always comes last.

## Separable verbs: a noun goes either place, a pronoun goes in the middle
If the object is a noun, it can come after the particle or between the verb and the particle:
> She **turned down** the offer. = She **turned** the offer **down**.
> Could you **switch off** the lights? = Could you **switch** the lights **off**?
If the object is a **pronoun** (it, them, him, her, me, us), it **must** go in the middle:
> She turned **it** down. (~~She turned down it.~~)
> I'll pick **them** up at six.
> Please fill **it** in. (~~fill in it~~)

## A long object goes after the particle
When the object is long or contains a clause, we usually put it after the particle because it is easier to read.
> The manager **brought up** the issue that had been ignored for years.
> ~~The manager brought the issue that had been ignored for years up.~~ — grammatical but awkward.
Short nouns can go either way: *call off the match / call the match off*.

## Inseparable verbs: the object comes last
Prepositional verbs and three-word verbs are not separated, even by a pronoun.
> We're looking **after** them. (~~We're looking them after.~~)
> They didn't put **up with** it. (~~put it up with~~)
> We ran **out of** milk. — Is there any left? — No, we ran **out of** it yesterday. (~~We ran out it of.~~)
A small group of three-word verbs take two objects: **put sth down to sb/sth** (to explain by), **take sb up on** (to accept an offer), **let sb in on** (to tell a secret). The first object (often a pronoun) goes between the verb and the particle: *I'll take you up on that offer.*

## Testing separability and clauses
- A good test: add *it*. If *turn it down* sounds right, the verb is separable; if *look it after* sounds wrong, it is not.
- One verb in two meanings may behave differently: *He ran up the hill* (a preposition, not separable) and *He ran up a huge bill* (a phrasal verb: *ran a huge bill up* is possible).
- In questions and relative clauses, the particle or preposition stays with the verb: *What are you looking for?* — *the offer we turned down* — *the problem we came up against.*
- In the passive, the particle stays with the verb: *The offer was turned down.* — *The children are looked after by their grandmother.*

## Common mistakes
- ~~She turned down it.~~ → She turned **it** down.
- ~~He picked up her.~~ → He picked **her** up.
- ~~look them after~~ → look **after them**
- ~~We ran out it of.~~ → We ran **out of** it.
- ~~I can't put up it with.~~ → I can't put **up with it**.
structure:
## Типы глаголов и порядок слов
| Тип | Примеры | Существительное | Местоимение |
|---|---|---|---|
| Разделяемый фразовый | turn down, pick up, fill in, put off | turn down the offer / turn the offer down | turn it down |
| Неразделяемый (с предлогом) | look after, get over, depend on | look after the children | look after them |
| Трёхсловный | put up with, run out of, come up with | put up with the noise | put up with it |
| Непереходный | take off, show up, break down | — | — |

## Формулы
> verb + **it / them** + particle · verb + particle + **a long noun phrase**
> verb + particle + preposition + **object**
> take **you** up on · put **it** down to · let **him** in on

## Вопрос и придаточное
| Структура | Пример |
|---|---|
| вопрос | What are you looking for? |
| относительное | the offer (that) we turned down |
| пассив | The meeting was put off. |

exercises.title: Подставьте местоимение
exercises.instruction: Вставьте вместо выделенного слова нужное местоимение (it, them, her, him).

items.text: The offer was too low, so she turned {{it}} down. (the offer)
I don't know that word. I'll look {{it}} up in a dictionary. (the word)
Your shoes are muddy. Take {{them}} off before you come in. (the shoes)
She read the recipe aloud while I wrote {{it}} down. (the recipe)
The children were noisy, but the nanny looked after {{them}} patiently. (the children)
The meeting is on Monday, but they've put {{it}} off until Friday. (the meeting)
These forms are confusing. Could you help me fill {{them}} in? (the forms)
I hadn't seen Ms Taylor for years, but I ran into {{her}} at the station yesterday.
I can't put {{up}} with this noise any longer.
We've run {{out}} of coffee, so I'll go to the shop.
She came {{up}} with a brilliant solution to the problem.
The students are looking forward {{to}} the end of the exams.
He got {{away}} with cheating for a whole year before anyone noticed.
Some people look {{down}} on those who haven't been to university.
She gets {{on|along}} well with her new boss.
The plane took {{off}} two hours late because of fog.

items.why: Местоимение в разделяемом глаголе стоит между глаголом и частицей.

options: Look up it in the dictionary.
Look it up in the dictionary.
Look it in the dictionary up.

items.why: Местоимение нельзя ставить после частицы: **turned it down**.

options: We ran out it of sugar.
items.why: Трёхсловный глагол **run out of** не разделяется.

options: The plan, which we came up with, worked.
The plan, which we came with up, worked.
The plan, which we came up, worked with.
items.why: В придаточном частица и предлог остаются при глаголе: **came up with**.

options: The manager brought the issue that had been ignored for years up.
The manager brought up the issue that had been ignored for years.
The manager up brought the issue that had been ignored for years.
items.why: Очень длинное дополнение ставят после частицы.

options: She put down to bad luck the failure.
She put the failure down to bad luck.
She put the failure to down bad luck.
items.why: **put sth down to sth** — дополнение стоит между глаголом и частицей.

items.why: Местоимение после частицы нельзя: **looked it up**.

exercises.title: Замените существительное местоимением
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, заменив выделенную часть местоимением.

answers: I'll pick her up at six.
I will pick her up at six.

exercises.title: Расставьте слова
exercises.instruction: Составьте предложение из слов. Если возможно несколько порядков, подойдёт любой верный.

answers: She looks after her little brother.
We have run out of milk.

items.prompt: (with / I / can't / this noise / put up)
answers: I can't put up with this noise.
I cannot put up with this noise.
The thief got away with it.

items.prompt: Describe your morning routine. Use at least two phrasal verbs (get up, turn off, put on...).
items.sample: I get up at seven, turn off the alarm and put on my running shoes.

items.prompt: Tell about something you had to put off. Use **put off**.
items.sample: I had to put off my dentist appointment because of work.

items.prompt: Is there anything you can't put up with? Use **put up with**.
items.sample: I can't put up with people who are always late.

items.prompt: What is something you have run out of recently? Use **run out of**.
items.sample: I ran out of coffee this morning.

items.prompt: Who do you look after, or who looks after you? Use **look after**.
items.sample: I look after my grandmother on weekends.
